definitions.explanation: The natural progression or development of a situation; how things turn out.
Letting events unfold naturally without active intervention.

examples.japanese: {成|な}り{行|ゆ}きを{見守|みまも}る。
examples.english: To watch how things develop./To wait and see.

examples.japanese: {成|な}り{行|ゆ}きに{任|まか}せる。
examples.english: To let things take their course.

examples.japanese: {成|な}り{行|ゆ}きで{付|つ}き{合|あ}うことになった。
examples.english: We ended up dating by circumstance./Things just happened that way.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{成|な}り (becoming) + {行|ゆ}き (going) → how things become/go = course of events

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{成|な}り{行|ゆ}きを{見守|みまも}る - to watch how things develop
・{成|な}り{行|ゆ}きに{任|まか}せる - to let things take their course
・{成|な}り{行|ゆ}きで - by circumstance, as things happened
・{成|な}り{行|ゆ}き{次第|しだい} - depending on how things go

FINANCE USAGE:
{成|な}り{行|ゆ}き{注文|ちゅうもん} refers to a "market order" in stock trading—buying or selling at the current market price rather than a specific price.

NUANCE:
Suggests a passive approach, letting events unfold naturally rather than actively controlling them. Can imply either wise patience or lack of initiative depending on context.
